points.evidence: Original returns from failed context allocation first, then allocates buffer32 but retests context. malloc_w can return NULL. It therefore bypasses existing WSAENOBUFS cleanup and supplies NULL with a nonzero buffer length. The original host/protocol/service async workers copy result structures into that buffer;this is a concrete invalid-buffer counterexample,not a conjectured scheduling race.
points.minimum: Keep one operand substitution;no helper or parallel path.

points.evidence: Original native WSAStartup is process-wide;task cleanup does not terminate the provider. Global async records have no task owner;original post conversion writes vBuffer16 before PostMessage validates the window. Existing task serial identifies the cleanup subset;uninitialized nonzero retirement flags could suppress a live completion. Each of the six real constructors initializes exactly once before submission.
points.minimum: Keep two direct assignments;no new ID or table. Complete rundown algorithm remains separately reviewed at R1797.

points.evidence: FindAndRemoveAsyncContext deliberately returns NULL after retired-task completion or after an already-removed cancellation. All three original completion functions only ASSERT nonnull,then access context on both success and message-post paths. In the selected PROD build the ASSERT does not stop this dereference. The same lookup owner must tell the converter to stop;adding a second context registry would duplicate ownership.
points.minimum: Keep the three-line NULL return. R1781 redundant explanation removed;R1786/R1791 already use that minimal readable form.
